title: Pending Release (ZIFFER-SPEC-001 §9.6, DR-1 / DR-4 / DR-6 / DR-9; ZIFFER-DEPLOY-001 DP-48)
description:
One floor-HIGH action, verified and HELD between §9.3 and execution. Committed by the Executor as S1 of the leg register (ZIFFER-DEPLOY-001 Annex A), which carries it among the Executor-local durable commits and not among the legs. F5.1 was its identifier while the register read it as a leg; ACP-86 retired that id, because an Executor-internal hold crosses no domain boundary and DP-83 makes a leg a crossing.

S1 IS AN EXECUTOR-INTERNAL HOLD, AND THAT CHANGES WHAT THIS SCHEMA IS FOR. Every other artifact in this directory crosses between two parties. This one does not: the register records it as a commit whose component column reads "Executor" and which names no crossing, so nothing here is received, and no field is class T in the sense §14 suite 12 means it -- a value transmitted by the party under verification. Every value below was verified by the Executor at §9.3, recomputed by it (TR-8, RV-3), or drawn by it (DR-11); the one exception is `notified`, and it is called out on the field. What the schema constrains is therefore DURABLE STATE, and that state is normative because DP-48 makes it so: an Executor MUST record entry into `pending_release` before the hold begins, and on recovery MUST enumerate every held action, void each with a critical alert and an audit record, and MUST NOT resume, re-time, or release any of them. A hold that lives only in process memory is a hold an ordinary restart erases -- along with a repudiation (DR-4) that has already arrived.

WHY THE HOLD EXISTS AT ALL. §9.3 establishes that a receipt is authentic, bound, fresh and quorum-satisfying. It cannot establish that the approvers SAW the action they approved. DR-1 therefore forbids a floor-HIGH action from executing at verification time and holds it while a summary rendered independently from the canonical bytes is delivered out of band (DR-2, DR-3) and any recipient may veto (DR-4). That raises the bar from one compromised component to two independent ones. A-8 is not closed and is not claimed to be.

WHAT IS BOUND TO WHAT, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE RECORD. A release must not be re-pointable at a different action, so the record pins three things and not one. `proposal_hash` names the action -- and it is a NAME, not evidence: at release the Executor re-hashes the bytes it is about to execute and compares (9.3-3, "the Executor hashes what it will execute -- never whatever the receipt describes"). `receipt_nonce` pins the ONE receipt whose quorum authorized this hold, because a Proposal can have more than one live receipt (DS-3 re-drives through a NEW attestation; DS-6a fixes the action identity across them), and a hold keyed only on the Proposal would let a later receipt inherit a hold -- and a veto -- raised against an earlier one. `policy_bundle_hash` and `bundle_epoch` name the signed policy the recomputations were made against, so `reversibility`, which decides whether silence releases, is something an auditor can reproduce rather than an assertion they must accept.

THE FIELD SET IS CLOSED, AND THE REASON IS NOT AT-8b's. `required` lists every property and `additionalProperties` is false, but Z4's argument does not carry over unchanged: nothing hashes this record, so two encodings of it do not become two ids and two ledger slots. What does carry over is the other half of it. An optional field is a field the release path sometimes reads as absent, the absent branch is the one nothing exercises, and here that branch decides whether an IRREVERSIBLE action releases with no acknowledgement. `acknowledged_by` and `repudiated_by` are therefore REQUIRED and MAY be empty arrays: an empty array is the honest encoding of "nobody did", where an omitted field is the same state spelled a second way. And DP-48's recovery path has to enumerate these records after a restart, which it cannot do faithfully for a record carrying a field it does not know about.

`x-acp-absent` APPEARS NOWHERE BELOW, DELIBERATELY. An absent rule answers "what does the SIGNED POLICY say when a lookup misses", and this record is not policy -- `tools/codegen.py` states that as a rule for the whole wire root, because a default supplied by the party under verification is not a fail-safe. RV-1's absent-from-`reversibility.json` default (IRREVERSIBLE) lives at the lookup, in `spec/schemas/bundle/reversibility.schema.json`, which is where it has effect. Restating it here would give one fail-safe two homes.

WHAT IS NOT A FIELD. (a) `release_at`: it is `held_at` plus `hold_window_seconds`, and a stored instant that can disagree with its own inputs is a second definition of one moment; the disagreement that matters is the early one, which is DR-1's refusal bypassed by a value rather than by a clock. (b) `release_mode`: DR-1 says it is determined by the recomputed reversibility class and the sampling draw, so it IS `reversibility` and `sampled`, computed at release and never stored -- stored, one flipped field converts a DR-9 hold into a DR-7 silent release. RV-4 does require the mode recorded, but in AUDIT, a different artifact on a different leg (F6.1). (c) `idempotency_key`: DS-6f pins `proposal_hash` to `origin_nonce` immutably in the Consumption Ledger and requires the Executor to READ origin from that binding and derive the key from what it read; a key copied in here would be read at the target call instead, which is Z3 one layer in -- the membership-versus-pinning distinction that let a compromised KMS move an idempotency key and double a floor-HIGH action. (d) A Context snapshot or a stored capability decision: 9.3 step 9 is a RE-QUERY written to close the issuance-to-execution window (T-10), a capability read before the hold is stale by the whole window, and carrying one would invite exactly the read that step forbids. (e) The Attestation Objects, their signatures, and their `attestation_id`s: the quorum was decided at 9.3 step 7b and the ids were consumed in the ledger (CL-3, AT-5), and re-deciding it at release against a copy this record supplied is a verification with no fresh binding. The attester IDENTITIES are kept, because DR-3 and DR-5 need to know who must be notified and who may veto. (f) The canonical Proposal bytes: where an Executor keeps what it is about to execute is a storage question the specification does not answer; what it does answer is that the hash of those bytes is recomputed and compared (9.3-3).

WHAT THIS SCHEMA DOES NOT CONSTRAIN. Almost everything that matters about a hold is a relation -- between fields, between times, or between components -- and JSON Schema expresses none of them: that the window has elapsed (DR-1), that the receipt has not expired during it (DR-6), that `notified` covers every attester and the operator (DR-3, DR-8), that an acknowledgement came from a notified non-operator (DR-9, DR-5), that a non-empty `repudiated_by` is terminal (DR-4), that `held_at` plus `hold_window_seconds` still leaves a processing margin inside the receipt's validity (DR-6). A record can be schema-valid and unreleasable, and a record can be schema-valid and MUST NOT release. This document constrains shape, and shape is not authority.

Two limits stated rather than left to be assumed. DR-2's render-path distinctness is a property of two CODE PATHS and cannot be a property of any object; nothing here can carry it, and the notifier self-certifying its own independence and coverage is the OPEN finding T-32 in ACP-CLASS-001. DR-11's requirement that the sampling draw come from a CSPRNG and be uninfluenceable by the requester is likewise unrepresentable: `sampled` records the OUTCOME of a draw and can say nothing about its source, so an implementation whose draw an attacker grinds against produces records that validate perfectly.

Finally, this record carries no signature and no integrity envelope, because the specification gives it none: its integrity is the Executor's own durable store. The closed field set above is a discipline about what the release path may read. It is not a defence against an Executor that writes whatever it likes.

proposal_hash.description: The canonical Proposal (JCS, WE-1) this action was authorized for. It is the name of the held action and not evidence of it: 9.3-3 requires the Executor to hash what it will execute and compare, and the hold is exactly the interval during which the thing to be executed and the thing that was approved can drift apart. Under DS-6f this is also the key of the immutable `proposal_hash` to `origin_nonce` ledger binding, which is where the idempotency key comes from at the target call -- not from anything recorded here.

receipt_nonce.description:
The `nonce` of the ONE receipt whose quorum authorized this hold, claimed in the Consumption Ledger at 9.3 step 6.

WHY THE RECORD NEEDS IT AND `proposal_hash` IS NOT ENOUGH. DS-3 re-drives an `indeterminate` outcome through a NEW attestation and therefore a new receipt, and DS-6a fixes the action identity across re-drives, so one Proposal can have several receipts alive inside a retention window. A hold identified only by its Proposal is a hold any of them can be released against -- including one whose attesters were never notified under DR-3, which detaches the DR-4 veto from the authorization it was raised against.

THE TYPE IS TWO RULES AND THEY REFUSE UNDER DIFFERENT NAMES. `b64:` plus the RFC 4648 §4 alphabet WITH padding is WE-4, the wire type, and the prefix is part of the value: it is carried, hashed and signed as that string, and stripping it, dropping the padding, or substituting the URL-safe alphabet each produce a different value and MUST be rejected rather than normalized. The twenty-two characters are L-17's 128 bits. A verifier folding the two into one check answers `WE-4` for a 64-bit nonce, which is a perfectly well-formed `b64:` value -- the wrong clause name, and the cross-language differential compares names. `tools/nonce-type-vectors.json` pins that pair for the ATTESTATION nonce across three implementations after they had already diverged for a release with every gate green; the receipt nonce has the same two rules and no such corpus.

receipt_expires_at.description: The verified receipt's `expires_at`, copied at 9.3 step 5 so DR-6 can be evaluated at release without re-reading the receipt. DR-6: release MUST fail closed if the receipt expired during the window, because a hold that outlives its authorization executes on an expired receipt, and L-14's 120 s ceiling exists to bound exactly that. Note what this value's authority rests on and what it does not: step 5 enforced the window LENGTH itself rather than reading it from the KMS-written value (Y2), and nothing re-derives it here -- this is a copy of a checked value, kept because the checker and the release step are separated by the hold.

policy_bundle_hash.description: The signed bundle established at 9.3 step 4, under which the values below were recomputed. It authorizes nothing at release -- no clause reads policy through this hash -- and it is here because a recomputation with no named input is not reproducible: RV-4 requires the recomputed reversibility class recorded in audit, and an auditor who cannot name the bundle cannot check the class or the release mode it selected.

bundle_epoch.description: Epoch of that bundle (9.3 step 4, which requires it be at least the Executor's last-seen epoch). Monotonicity is enforced at the KMS against a durable high-water mark (RAD-3) and, across a restart, against the Executor's own recovered mark (DP-47) -- never from this value. It is recorded so that a hold raised under epoch N is still visibly a hold raised under epoch N after a rotation, which is the only way to read a release decision made under a bundle that is no longer current.

tenant_id.description: The tenant scope verified at 9.3 step 8, where the receipt's tenant must match the tenant scope of the credentials about to be used. Three obligations need it at release rather than at verification: DR-12 counts silent releases in a PER-TENANT counter, DR-13 counts its below-HIGH notices as a separate class in the same discipline, and AU-2 makes `(tenant_id, seq)` unique and gapless in the audit chain. A release that cannot name its tenant cannot be counted and cannot be anchored.

operator.description: The operator identity taken from the VERIFIED Attestation Objects at 9.3 step 7b(iii-a) -- never from the receipt body's `operator`, which is diagnostic only (Y4). Three rules read it during the hold. DR-3 makes the operator a required notification recipient alongside every attester. DR-9 refuses an acknowledgement from the operator: the party who initiated the action carries no independent information about whether the displayed summary was honest, which is AT-2's approver-distinctness restated at the release step. And 9.3 step 9 rechecks capability on this identity, which is why it must be the signature-covered one.

attesters.description:
Every attester recorded in the verified Attestation Objects. DR-3 requires the notification to reach each of them and the operator, over a channel distinct from the one that obtained approval; DR-5 accepts a repudiation or an acknowledgement only from a party recorded as notified.

IT IS KEPT AS THE RECOMPUTED HALF OF THAT PAIR. The set of parties who MUST be notified is derived from signatures the Executor itself verified, so DR-8's completeness test can compare `notified` against this rather than asking the notification service who its audience should have been. Asking the notifier is the shape of T-32, still OPEN in ACP-CLASS-001: a service that selects and then certifies its own coverage is verifying itself.

`minItems` is 2 because L-16 puts the floor-HIGH quorum at two distinct attesters, each distinct from the operator, and a floor-HIGH receipt with no attestations fails closed at INV-1-HIGH before any hold exists. `uniqueItems` compares identity STRINGS, which is deliberately the weaker check: AT-2 distinctness is resolved over registry KEYS and not over names (PB-7, where changing a `role` string let one key holder satisfy a k=2 quorum alone), and that resolution happened at 9.3 step 7b(vi). This constraint restates none of it.

floor_only_risk.description:
The recomputed floor-only risk that put this action on the deferred path. The `const` is DR-1's scope made checkable: DR-1 defers an action whose RECOMPUTED floor-only risk is HIGH, and DR-13 states in as many words that DR-1 through DR-12 govern that path only -- an irreversible action below HIGH takes the notice path instead, which is a different artifact on a different path -- the Executor-local commit S2, whose leg id F5.6 ACP-86 retired for the same reason as F5.1's. A `pending_release` record graded anything else is a record that should not exist.

IT IS HERE TO BE REFUSED ON, NOT RELIED ON. TR-8 admits one source for a risk grade: recomputation from the signed bundle's floors and risk functions applied to the independently received canonical Proposal, ignoring Context-Store raises and ignoring any transmitted value. Nothing at release may read this field as the grade. Reading a stored grade instead of recomputing is X1 -- a forged `risk_level_floor_only` suppressing attestation -- with the storage moved inside the verifier.

reversibility.description:
The class RECOMPUTED at verification from the trusted bundle and the Proposal's `task_type` (RV-3), never read from the receipt: a receipt-asserted `REVERSIBLE` would suppress the DR-9 acknowledgement requirement exactly as v1.3.0's forged `risk_level_floor_only` suppressed attestation, same defect class and a different field. RV-2 puts the class in the signed bundle only -- no Context raise, no runtime override, no receipt field of record -- and makes downgrading one as dangerous a policy operation as lowering a tier floor (RK-5).

With `sampled` it decides the release mode (DR-1), and the two outcomes are not variations on one control. `IRREVERSIBLE` requires positive acknowledgement from a notified non-operator and TIMES OUT CLOSED (DR-9). `REVERSIBLE` releases on silence, and only there, because a control whose default outcome equals its approved outcome teaches its own users to ignore it and decays into a log entry while the dashboard still reports that human oversight exists (DR-7).

RV-1's absent-from-`reversibility.json` default is IRREVERSIBLE, and it belongs to the LOOKUP, not to this field: it is carried by `spec/schemas/bundle/reversibility.schema.json`'s `x-acp-absent` and generated into the table's accessor. This field is required and has no default.

IT IS THE BUNDLE'S TYPE, NOT A SECOND ONE. This field `$ref`s `spec/schemas/bundle/reversibility.schema.json#/$defs/reversibility` across roots. It was declared twice until ACP-78 M1 -- `ReversibilityClass` here beside the bundle's `Reversibility` -- on the argument that signed policy and a recorded value are never interchangeable (RES-8) and the module a reader holds should say which they have. That argument is right about the VALUE and wrong about the TYPE: what carries the provenance is the object the value sits in, a signed `reversibility.json` against a transmitted record, and a two-case vocabulary duplicated is two definitions of one object. RV-3 also has to COMPARE the recomputed class against the table it came from, and a comparison between two enums that merely look alike is the CR-4 defect one artifact down.

sampled.description:
The DR-10 confirmation-sampling draw for this action. A bundle-configured fraction of REVERSIBLE floor-HIGH actions (L-29, default 10%) inherits DR-9's acknowledgement duty, for a reason about people rather than cryptography: if recipients learn that reversible actions never require a response they stop reading those notifications too, and the channel decays for the class that is most of the traffic.

DR-11 governs the draw and none of it is visible here. It MUST come from a cryptographically secure source at the Executor or an equivalently isolated component; it MUST NOT be derived from the Proposal, the operator identity, or any requester-supplied value, because a derived draw is one an attacker grinds inputs against until the action falls outside the sample; and it MUST be recorded so the realised rate is verifiable after the fact. This field is that record, and it is the OUTCOME only.

Because it is REQUIRED, the draw is made no later than the durable commit -- earlier than DR-10 demands, and out of reach of anything that happens during the hold. DR-10 scopes sampling to REVERSIBLE actions and the specification does not say what the value means for an IRREVERSIBLE one, where DR-9 already requires acknowledgement; there both `true` and `false` describe the same release mode.

held_at.description:
RFC 3339 instant at which the action entered `pending_release` and the window started (DR-1). DP-48 makes it the moment the DURABLE record must already exist by -- "before the hold begins" is the whole of that clause's ordering, and it is AU-7's anchor-before-release rule applied to the Executor's own state, for the same reason: a record written after the fact can be suppressed by whatever the action enabled.

Evaluated against NTS-disciplined wall time within the L-20 skew allowance of five seconds, never against a monotonic clock. Leg F9.1 carries that dependency and DP-52 states the distinction. It matters more here than on a receipt: DR-6's margin between the end of the hold and the expiry of the receipt is measured across two components' clocks.

hold_window_seconds.description:
The window this action must survive before it may release, read from the SIGNED BUNDLE in force at 9.3 step 4 (DR-1; L-28: default 60 s, minimum 30 s). Release before it has elapsed MUST fail closed.

THE UPPER BOUND IS A REFUSAL, NOT A STYLE CHOICE. L-14 caps receipt validity at 120 s, so DR-6 makes a window at or above that ceiling an UNSATISFIABLE configuration -- no legal receipt can outlive it -- which MUST be rejected rather than silently never releasing. Testing found the interaction directly: a 60 s hold inside a 60 s receipt window expires mid-hold and never releases the honest path. `maximum` is inclusive and this repository's generator carries no exclusive bound, so 119 is "strictly below the ceiling" written in the only keyword available. It is the loosest value the specification permits and emphatically not a safe one: DR-6's actual requirement is `hold_window + processing margin < receipt validity`, the margin is a property of the deployment, and no schema can check it.

Two choices here are this schema's and not the specification's, and both are recorded rather than hidden. L-28 states the window in seconds but nowhere states its granularity; integer seconds is a decision. And pinning the window IN the record rather than re-reading it from the bundle at release is a decision too -- it stops a rotation during the hold from retroactively lengthening or shortening a window the attesters were notified about -- on a question §9.6 does not answer.

notified.description:
The parties the notification service reported delivering to. DR-3 requires that to be every attester in the verified Attestation Objects and the operator, over a channel distinct from the one used to obtain approval. Two clauses then read this set: DR-8, where an unreachable recipient or any failed delivery means the action MUST NOT release, because executing while the detection channel is absent is executing unwatched; and DR-5, where an acknowledgement or a repudiation is accepted ONLY from a party recorded here, or a compromised presentation service suppresses the veto the mechanism exists to enable.

THIS IS THE ONE VALUE IN THE RECORD THE EXECUTOR NEITHER VERIFIED NOR RECOMPUTED. It is the notifier's claim about its own coverage, which is RES-8's shape and the OPEN finding T-32 in ACP-CLASS-001, where `delivered` is classified T against a disclosed residual. `attesters` sits beside it so DR-8's completeness test compares this claim against a set derived from verified signatures instead of against the notifier's own answer about who its audience should have been.

MAY BE EMPTY, and the empty case is not slack. DP-48 requires the durable record to exist BEFORE the hold begins while DR-3's delivery happens DURING it, so a committed, not-yet-delivered record is a state the specification's own ordering produces. What may be done with such a record -- how long it may sit undelivered, whether an undelivered hold expires or is voided -- §9.6 does not say.

acknowledged_by.description:
Notified parties that positively acknowledged during the window. Where the recomputed reversibility class is IRREVERSIBLE, DR-9 requires at least one such acknowledgement before release and TIMES OUT CLOSED -- a timed-out action needs a fresh quorum, never a replay. DR-10 gives sampled REVERSIBLE actions the same duty. The acknowledgement MUST NOT come from the operator (DR-9), which is why `operator` is carried in this record rather than looked up later.

Empty is the ordinary state on the DR-7 silent path, and it is not free: DR-12 requires every release with an empty set here to increment a per-tenant counter recorded in audit, so that silence is a MEASURABLE DEBT rather than an invisible acknowledgement, and deployments SHOULD alert on the rate rather than merely record it.

WHAT AN IDENTITY IN THIS ARRAY IS NOT. The reference-level ACK-1..ACK-6 rules make each acknowledgement a signed, closed-schema, single-use object bound to `proposal_hash` and verified against a registered key (leg F5.4). This field records only the identities that survived those checks. An identity is not evidence of the object it came from, and nothing downstream may treat it as one.

repudiated_by.description:
Notified parties that repudiated during the window (DR-4, DR-5). Any notified party MAY repudiate; repudiation MUST fail closed with a critical alert; consumed attestations remain consumed, so a repudiated action requires a fresh quorum and never a replay. A non-empty array is therefore TERMINAL for this record: no later acknowledgement and no elapsed window releases it.

An array rather than a nullable identity, because `null` and an omitted field are one state spelled two ways -- Z4's argument at the record layer, where the cost is an unexercised branch in the release path rather than a second ledger slot, and where the branch decides whether a veto is seen. The empty array means nobody repudiated, and it means it in exactly one way.
